newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar drops on slow demand, profit-booking.
newsitem.headline: India sugar drops on slow demand, profit-booking.

text.p: Sugar prices dropped further on the local market on Monday as sluggish consumer demand pulled prices lower while stockists were booking profits at the higher level, dealers said.
In ready delivery sugar S-30 slid by 8/23 rupees at 1,420/1,440 rupees per quintal while M-30 sugar was steady at 1,450/1,500 rupees per quintal amid limited arrivals and shortage of ready stock.
Sugar mill delivery on the other hand moved down to 1,360/1,370 rupees per quintal from 1,365/1,375 rupees.

"Outstation buying at the mill level remained slow today but offerings by millers also remained at a low ebb as most millers have sold out their free sale quota for the current month," one broker said.
Free sale quota for the current month is 800,000 tonnes against 750,000 tonnes released last month. The quota for the next month is 800,000 tonnes.
Overall sentiment remained quiet and traders expect prices to move in a narrow band over the next few days.
